chunks: 4493 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Ḥumrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a man who married a virgin bondwoman who had not yet reached maturity; then when he consummated the marriage with her, he deflowered her and caused ifḍāʾ.

He said: “If he consummated the marriage with her when she was nine years old, then there is nothing upon him. But if she had not reached nine years, or was slightly less than that when he consummated the marriage with her and deflowered her, then he has indeed harmed her and rendered her unavailable to husbands. So it is upon the Imam to impose upon him her indemnity. But if he keeps her and does not divorce her until she dies, then there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.أَفْسَدَهَا: he caused lasting harm to her
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the authority who enforces the ruling
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a young bondwoman or female slave
key_terms.فَأَفْضَاهَا: he caused ifḍāʾ, a severe bodily injury through intercourse
key_terms.لَمْ تُدْرِكْ: she had not yet reached maturity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia fiqh on causing ifḍāʾ to a wife who is under nine years old?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning injury caused through consummation of marriage with a girl below the age of nine. It distinguishes between consummation at nine years and below that age, and states financial liability and the Imam's role in enforcement in the latter case. It is a jurisprudential text related to marriage law, bodily harm, and judicial authority.
